title: GF(65521)/n=64 blocked solve kernel (6613abf4 rows 55, 56 follow-up)
description:
Phase 6 follow-up filed under epic `026fc832`. Predecessor: `6613abf4` (blocked triangular solve R0 closed 7/13 PASS; rows 55, 56 routed here).

## Background

The `6613abf4` blocked triangular solve closes 7 of 13 A8 solve cells but FAILs rows 55 + 56 at GF(65521)/n=64 (2.10× and 1.83×). Root cause documented at `dev/bench_results/2026-05-26-6613abf4-blocked-solve.md` § 7: at n=64 with the `TRSM_BLOCKED_PANEL_SIZE = 64` threshold, the blocked-TRSM dispatch is not active (n is exactly the threshold; per-panel update GEMM shape is too small for the medium-prime u16 packed kernel). The medium-prime u16 path also doesn't activate at the per-cell-dot level because the criterion in `gemm_axpy_into_view` for the u16 kernel is similar.

Sibling cells GF(65521)/n=256 and n=1024 PASS (rows 57-58 at 1.247×, 1.210×). The structural gap is specifically for the n=64 / medium-prime / single-column-RHS regime.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A blocked solve dispatch path for GF(65521)/n=64 that closes both rows 55 (uniform) and 56 (deficient) at ≤ 1.5× vs fflas, OR carries explicit user-approved [aspirational] amendment for each cell.
- [hard] No regression on currently-PASSing GF(65521) cells (delta ≤ 5%, paired tight-session bench).
- [hard] Bit-exact correctness preserved (reuse `prop_blocked_solve_boundary_sweep_fp65521` at the existing inverse.rs location).
- [hard] No `unsafe` outside kernel crates.

## Out of scope

- GF(251)/n=64 cells (covered by separate borderline investigation task).
- Non-medium-prime solve paths.
- Echelon and invert ops (sibling wave-7b issues).
